items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1960-11-18
items.q: And we'd travel around Mississippi and parts of Louisiana with Ridgely

ctx.x: Was Keith going bad or why did he stop trombone, do you know?

Well no I don't know why he stopped trombone but when he was playing drums I think Gilbert Young was the one who got me with the band. Gilbert Young and Emma Barrett the bell girl, she was playing piano and Feliks Goff was playing tenor saxophone because sometime Mr. Porter, Feliks would take a solo on a clap and Mr. Porter grab his tenor saxophone and he'd be playing and let it blow by and you know one of them kind of things. He could play at saxophone too you know Mr. Porter. Yeah. And we'd travel around…
I was going to ask one more question about Ridgely, did they both call it the Tuxedo Band? Is there any trouble about that? Yeah.

items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1960-10-14
items.q: He used to play with Rizzly, when we were playing with Rizzly, old man Porter was playing who the former was, with Rizzly.

ctx.x: He could talk in 15 minutes all right, too.

Yeah, right. See, he was playing with Sid and Desiree in a long time, he and my brother like Tom Johnson. But Tom's in California, too, a very good saxophone player. We had a saxophone, a clarinet player, was a very, very good, well, actually, if you've ever heard of it, by the name of Felix Goff. He used to play with Rizzly, when we were playing with Rizzly, old man Porter was playing who the former was, with Rizzly. And this boy named Felix Goff, he could play. Man, he could play some time. I thought, you know,…
Sam, you know, we talked to brother, you see.
